summary: R27.1 + R28 + R28.1 refinements validated end-to-end. Backend: 13/13 in-process pytest (test_ssot_persistence.py) + 9/9 live pytest against preview URL (new test_ssot_r28_live.py). Frontend: SSOT case restored via CasesDrawer → 0 /api/die/* calls, 0 r28_violation telemetry pings, compound version ribbon 'SSOT 1.0 · legacy · phase1 · R27 · no recomputation', ArtifactTracePanel renders with correct Artifact→Recognizer→Capability→Evidence rows, SSOT badge visible.

ui_bugs.issue: Runtime crash `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toUpperCase')` at AcquisitionPlanPanel.jsx:178 when a restored SSOT's investigation_object.acquisition_plan contains any step without an `id` field. The panel's step.id.toUpperCase() should be defensively guarded (step?.id?.toUpperCase?.() || `STEP-${i}`) so a malformed/legacy SSOT can't take down the whole workspace and also block the sibling ArtifactTracePanel from rendering.

action_items: OPTIONAL — Defensively guard AcquisitionPlanPanel.jsx line 178: `step?.id?.toUpperCase?.() ?? "STEP-"+i`. Currently a malformed acquisition_plan entry (missing `id`) crashes the entire workspace during SSOT restore, which also prevents ArtifactTracePanel (rendered as sibling under the panel) from ever appearing. Reproducible by posting an SSOT with investigation_object.acquisition_plan = [{step:"iocs"}] to /api/cases/save and clicking OPEN.

OPTIONAL — The status ribbon container does not carry a stable data-testid (had to fall back to text probe for `OPENED` substring). Adding data-testid="workspace-status" or "status-ribbon" would make regression tests robust.
critical_code_review_comments: R28 · Restore is Rendering guard (frontend/src/lib/api.js:60-118) is correctly wired: request interceptor calls _r28_check(config.url); forbidden patterns match /die/*, /decode/*, /analyze/*, /ai/*, /troubleshoot/*; telemetry ping is non-blocking via fetch+keepalive. Live test confirms zero pings during a real SSOT restore.

R28.1 · services/ssot_store.py cleanly separates concerns: build_version_stamp / coerce_version / canonical_bytes / compute_checksum / store_ssot / load_ssot / project_artifact_trace. canonical_bytes scrubs persisted_at + pointer fields so content-hash is stable across saves — confirmed by dedupe test (two saves w/ same ssot → same investigation_id + checksum).

routers/ssot.py only imports load_ssot + project_artifact_trace (AST-verified by test_ssot_endpoint_does_not_touch_business_logic). No decoder, classifier, AI enricher, or preprocessor referenced. R28 contract honoured.

cases.py save→GET round-trip: ssot_source='immutable_store' when ssot_ref exists; artifact_trace populated at read time from the resolved SSOT; ssot_ref carries {id, checksum (sha256 hex), version (compound dict)}.

WorkspacePage.jsx L3486-3533 wraps SSOT hydration with beginRestoreMode/endRestoreMode + try/finally + setTimeout(endRestoreMode,0) so any state-effect-triggered fetches during the same tick are also gated. Confirmed no /die/* calls during live restore.

ArtifactTracePanel.jsx renders `null` when trace is empty (correct — no phantom panels on legacy cases) and shows the exact header specified by the contract: `▸ ARTIFACT TRACE · Artifact → Recognizer → Capability → Evidence`.
Non-blocker · WorkspacePage.jsx is 3667 lines (up from 3631 in iteration_68) — refactor into hooks (useCaseHydration, useAutoInvestigate) recommended for maintainability.

Non-blocker · CasesDrawer displays `🔒 SSOT v1.0` (bare schema version). Since backend now serves the compound stamp on the case doc's ssot_ref.version, the drawer could show the full stamp (or at least the baseline like `SSOT · R27`) to differentiate cases saved under different pipeline generations post-UAIE.
